movesLifeStageScale.citation: Scales the American Community Survey 2024 rate of leaving the county for a person's age band and state (data/research/migration/mover-rates-acs-2024.json) into their monthly pull to leave, so that a town's departures over a year, after each person's own ties hold some back, land on that rate. Calibrated in src/core2/moves.test.ts.

spread.unit: multiple of the ACS departure rate
spread.citation: Checked range, not a measure: the year run (scripts/research/core-parameters-year.ts) reports a town's departures against the ACS 2024 rate for its adults' ages and state (data/research/migration/mover-rates-acs-2024.json).

movesOwnerHold.citation: How much owning the home holds a household in place: in the year to March 2023, 1.85% of people in owner-occupied homes moved to a different county against 6.23% of people in rented homes (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 1 'General Mobility in the Past Year', mig_01_2023_1yr.xlsx, rows 66-67, https://www.census.gov/data/tables/2023/demo/geographic-mobility/cps-2023.html); ln(6.23/1.85) = 1.21 (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json, checked by scripts/research/core-parameters-check.ts).
movesOwnerHold.estimatedFrom: The log of the renters' different-county move rate over the owners', because the hold is added on the log scale of the leaving rate. The two groups are compared without controls (owners are older), so it stands in for the hold of owning alone; a tenure effect net of age would make it SOURCED.

spread.citation: CPS ASEC 2023 Table 1: different county ln(6.23/1.85) = 1.21 to different state ln(2.78/0.74) = 1.32 (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesChildrenHold.citation: How much children under 18 at home hold a household in place; the size is a starting value. The published rates convert to 0.32: in the year to March 2023, 4.15% of family householders 15 to 54 with no own child under 18 moved to a different county against 3.03% of those with one (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 6, mig_06_2023_1yr.xlsx, rows 9-10, https://www.census.gov/data/tables/2023/demo/geographic-mobility/cps-2023.html); ln(4.15/3.03) = 0.32 (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json, checked by scripts/research/core-parameters-check.ts). The value stays at the starting 0.4 because the converted holds move src/core2/moves.test.ts past its departure band while the engine already sends more adults away than the ACS rate; world-town-net-moving-negative applies 0.32 once the departure rate is right.

spread.citation: Sourced outcome band, CPS ASEC 2023 Table 6 by the youngest child: under 6 only ln(4.15/5.26) = -0.24 (families with only young children move more) to 6 to 17 only ln(4.15/2.11) = 0.67; all own children under 18, 0.32 (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesKinHold.citation: How much each close relative living in town holds a person there, up to movesKinHoldCap relatives; the size is a starting value. The published effect converts to 0.30 per relative: having a sibling or extended relative within a mile cuts the odds of moving out of the neighborhood to 0.741 (parents 0.530, children 0.644; Spring, Ackert, Crowder and South 2017, Demography 54(4):1277-1304, Table 4, Model 2, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5734642/); ln(1/0.741) = 0.30 (data/research/core/spring-2017-kin-proximity.json, checked by scripts/research/core-parameters-check.ts). The study measures leaving the tract within a metro area, not the town. The value stays at the starting 0.15, below the band, because the converted holds move src/core2/moves.test.ts past its departure band while the engine already sends more adults away than the ACS rate; world-town-net-moving-negative applies 0.30 once the departure rate is right.

spread.unit: log odds per relative in town
spread.citation: Sourced outcome band, Spring et al. 2017 Table 4, 95 percent bounds from the printed standard errors: siblings or extended kin ln(1/0.786) = 0.24 to parents ln(1/0.489) = 0.72 (data/research/core/spring-2017-kin-proximity.json).

movesKinHoldCap.citation: How many relatives in town count toward holding a person there.

spread.citation: Checked range, not a measure. A cap: core-moves-caps-and-minimum-age-as-cause replaces it with a sliding hold.

movesJobHold.citation: How much a job holds a person in place: 3.66% of employed civilians moved to a different county in the year to March 2023 against 5.93% of the unemployed (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 2 'General Mobility by Labor Force Status', mig_02_2023_1yr.xlsx, rows 9 and 11, column I); ln(5.93/3.66) = 0.48 (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json, checked by scripts/research/core-parameters-check.ts). The unemployed sample is small (6.2 million people).
movesJobHold.estimatedFrom: The log of the unemployed's different-county move rate over the employed's, on the log scale the holds are added on, without controls; people not in the labor force move less than either (2.40%), so the hold is read against the unemployed only.

spread.citation: CPS ASEC 2023 Table 2: different county ln(5.93/3.66) = 0.48 to different state ln(3.10/1.54) = 0.70 (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesOfficeHold.citation: How much holding an office holds its holder in town: the strongest hold, above owning a home (movesOwnerHold, 1.21), because moving out of the district gives up the seat (an office becomes vacant when its holder ceases to be an inhabitant of the jurisdiction, e.g. California Government Code section 1770(e)). While they serve, an officeholder's pull builds only from recorded events, never from their stage of life.

spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it: no study measures how often officeholders leave their district; checked to sit above the owner hold.

movesEvictedPull.citation: The push an eviction adds toward leaving town, a third of the way to leaving. Most evicted families stay in their city, moving to poorer neighborhoods (Desmond and Shollenberger 2015, Demography 52(5):1751-1772), and 'foreclosure or eviction' is 0.7% of all movers' reasons and 0.10% of different-county movers' (11 of 10,480 thousand; Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json). Neither figure converts to the push: they say how few movers were evicted, not how many evicted people leave.

spread.unit: share of the way to leaving
spread.citation: Checked range around the starting value. The year run (scripts/research/core-parameters-year.ts) reports the share of leavers whose recorded causes include an eviction against the CPS different-county reason share (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesJobLostPull.citation: The push a lost job adds toward leaving town. 'To look for work or lost job' is 1.5% of all movers' reasons and 2.1% of different-county movers' (222 of 10,480 thousand; Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json), and most people who lose a job stay. The reason share says how few movers lost a job, not how many who lose one leave, so it does not convert to the push.

spread.unit: share of the way to leaving
spread.citation: Checked range around the starting value. The year run (scripts/research/core-parameters-year.ts) reports the share of leavers whose recorded causes include a job loss against the CPS different-county reason share (data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesKinMovedPull.citation: The push a parent, child or sibling moving away adds toward following them. 'Other family reason' is 7.9% of movers' reasons (Census CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13).

spread.unit: share of the way to leaving
spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it; the year run reports leavers following kin against the CPS intercounty 'other family reason' share (9.6%, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesStayPull.citation: What staying weighs against the built-up pull to leave in the monthly choice; the pull is measured on this scale.

spread.unit: the unit of the pull scale
spread.citation: The unit every pull and hold is measured in; it is not a measure of anything, and movesLifeStageScale sets how fast pulls build against it.

movesMinimumAge.citation: The youngest age band in the American Community Survey 2024 departure rates this engine reads (18 and 19); younger people move with their household.

movesRiskWeight.citation: How much a person's trait lean toward moving away over staying put (every trait through the shared trait table, about -1 to 1; OPUS-TRAITS, Oct 12, 2026) loosens what holds them in town (a lean toward staying tightens it). Personality predicts moving within and between US states (Jokela 2009, Journal of Research in Personality 43(1):79-83); the size is a starting value.

spread.unit: log scale of the holds per unit of trait lean
spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it here: Jokela 2009 (Journal of Research in Personality 43(1):79-83) was not reachable (sciencedirect.com HTTP 403); the trait effect it reports is held as moves.move-away in data/research/trait-effect-sizes.json (odds ratio 1.19 per SD for moving between states) for the trait calibration (scripts/traits/trait-calibrate.ts).

movesDaysPerYear.citation: Days in a calendar year: a job's daily wage times this, over the months in a year, is the household's monthly pay that its rent or mortgage is weighed against.

movesHousingCostWeight.citation: How much what a home costs, as a share of the household's income, pushes a person toward leaving town (at a share of 0.3 the push is 0.24 on the scale of the holds; at the cap it is 0.8). Renters paying more of their income for housing move more, and 'wanted cheaper housing' is one of the housing reasons movers give (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13); the size is a starting value.

spread.unit: log scale of the holds per share of income
spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it; the year run reports leavers with a housing-cost push against the CPS intercounty 'cheaper housing' share (7.3%, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesHousingCostShareCap.citation: The largest share of income a home's cost counts as when it pushes toward leaving; a household with no income at all reads as this share.

spread.citation: Checked range, not a measure. A cap: core-moves-caps-and-minimum-age-as-cause replaces it with a sliding push.

movesJobElsewherePush.citation: The push a job paid from another place adds toward moving nearer to it. 'New job or job transfer' and 'to be closer to work / easier commute' are among the work reasons movers give (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13); the size is a starting value.

spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it; the year run reports leavers with a job elsewhere against the CPS intercounty 'new job or job transfer' and 'closer to work' shares (23.0% and 5.3%, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesCloseElsewherePull.citation: The push toward leaving from a partner, parent or child living elsewhere, times how close the person is to them now (0 to 1 each, faded since their last contact; up to movesKinHoldCap of closeness). People move toward close kin (Spring, Ackert, Crowder and South 2017, Demography 54(4):1277-1304), and family reasons are the largest group of movers' reasons (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13); the size is a starting value.

spread.unit: log scale of the holds per unit of closeness
spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it; the year run reports leavers with close kin elsewhere against the CPS intercounty 'other family reason' share (9.6%, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesHouseholdLossPull.citation: The push a death at home (a partner or someone they live with) adds toward leaving town. 'Change in marital status' and other family reasons are a share of movers' reasons (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13); most widowed people stay, so the push is a quarter of the way to leaving.

spread.unit: share of the way to leaving
spread.citation: TUNABLE starting value; no published effect converts to it; the year run reports leavers after a death at home against the CPS intercounty 'change in marital status' share (4.9%, data/research/core/cps-asec-2023-mobility.json).

movesUnemploymentGapWeight.citation: How much each point of the region's unemployment above the nation's, beyond the gap it opened with, speeds everyone's pull to leave (and each point below slows it), as a share of the rate on the log scale. Net out-migration of about 0.25% of the population a year per point of relative unemployment (Blanchard and Katz 1992, BPEA; the regional engine's regionalMigrationPerUnemploymentPoint) over adults' county departure rate of about 5.8% a year (ACS 2024, data/research/migration/mover-rates-acs-2024.json): 0.25 / 5.8 = 0.043.
movesUnemploymentGapWeight.estimatedFrom: Blanchard and Katz 1992; Dao, Furceri and Loungani 2017 put the migration response at a quarter to a half of a local shock; spread 0.02 to 0.09

spread.unit: log change in the leaving rate per point of relative unemployment
spread.citation: Dao, Furceri and Loungani 2017 put the migration response at a quarter to a half of a local shock, against Blanchard and Katz 1992 (as the starting value states); not reopened in this research.
